title: Hydrogen-like species: wavelength ratio, atomic number and ionic charge
summary: Build a hydrogen-like ion proton by proton, fire tuned photons at it and watch the electron jump, hunt the pair of atomic numbers that makes one wavelength exactly nine times the other, then count the particles to turn Z into the ionic charge.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Bohr model of hydrogen-like species and the Rydberg equation
subtopics: Hydrogen-like species and the one-electron condition
Energy levels and the Z-squared scaling
Rydberg equation and the ratio of two wavelengths
concepts: Hydrogen-like means exactly one electron, not one proton
The Bohr result E = -13.6 Z^2 / n^2 holds only for a one-electron species
Dividing two Rydberg equations cancels the constant and the wavelength alike
Longer wavelength means lower photon energy, never higher
The charge on a hydrogen-like ion is Z - 1, so the question is one subtraction longer than it looks
formulas: lambda = hc / dE, so energy and wavelength are inversely related
n = 1 -> 2 factor = 3/4; n = 2 -> 4 factor = 3/16; their ratio = 4
charge = protons - electrons = Z - 1 for a hydrogen-like ion

methods: Derived from first principles before any published key was consulted: the one-electron condition, the two geometric factors, the ratio and the final subtraction were all fixed independently

The geometric factors computed as exact fractions rather than decimals: 1 - 1/4 = 3/4 and 1/4 - 1/16 = 3/16, whose quotient is exactly 4, so the condition is 4 Z_X^2 / Z_Y^2 = 9 with no rounding anywhere

Brute force over every integer pair with 1 <= Z <= 60: the pairs giving a wavelength ratio of exactly 9.000000 are (3,2), (6,4), (9,6), (12,8) and so on - every one in the ratio 3 : 2 and none outside it, with (3,2) the smallest

Two independent numerical routes agree: Bohr energies with the Rydberg energy 13.605693 eV give lambda_X = 13.5003 nm and lambda_Y = 121.5023 nm, and the Rydberg constant 1.0973732e7 per metre gives the same two numbers; their quotient is 9.0000000000
dE / Z^2 confirmed constant at 2.5511 eV across Z = 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 for the n = 2 -> 4 transition, which is the Z^2 scaling the whole argument rests on
Direction of the ratio checked: reversing it to Z_X : Z_Y = 2 : 3 gives 1.7778, and two hydrogen atoms give exactly 4 - neither is 9
Both ions confirmed to be genuinely positive at the minimum, a = 2 and b = 1, as the notation X(a+) and Y(b+) requires
a + b = 5m - 2 confirmed strictly increasing, so m = 1 is the minimum rather than an assumption
The printed traps reproduced deliberately: Z_X + Z_Y = 5 is a different number from a + b = 3, and dropping the factor of 4 would give the ratio 3 : 1 instead of 3 : 2

Answer cross-checked afterwards against a published worked solution for this paper, which reports the same intermediate values (Z_X = 3, Z_Y = 2, a = 2, b = 1) and the same answer, 3. IIT Roorkee's official key was not retrievable at the time of writing

Headless-browser run of the finished page: 88 assertions covering the ion foundry and its non-hydrogen-like refusal, the spectrometer with a deliberately mistuned photon passing through and a matched one being absorbed, the recorded absorption lines and the spectrum strip, the Z-squared chart, the ratio hunter locking only on multiples of (3,2), the self-stopping sweep, the charge tally, the m study staying blank until it is earned, the gate, badges, celebration, traps, progressive hints, teacher mode, theme toggle, clean console and zero horizontal overflow at 390 px and 360 px
verification.note: IIT Roorkee's official key was not retrievable; the published solution used for cross-checking is a coaching-institute solution that agrees with the independent derivation at every intermediate step, not only on the final number.

interactivity: Four benches, one per decision the question hides, each gated behind a prediction the student must commit to before the apparatus will settle anything
Ion foundry: a Z slider builds the nucleus proton by proton so the protons can actually be counted, with electrons stripped and replaced one at a time
The species is named live - H, He+, Li2+, Be3+ - and the drawing states plainly when Bohr's E = -13.6 Z^2/n^2 no longer applies because more than one electron is present
Claim A refuses to settle on a single species: two hydrogen-like species with different atomic numbers have to be built before the comparison can be made
Working absorption spectrometer: tuneable source, slit, sample chamber holding the ion, and a detector
The photon is drawn as a wave packet whose drawn wavelength and colour follow the energy actually selected, and it travels along the beam rather than appearing at its destination

Absorption is all-or-nothing: a mistuned photon flies through the sample to the detector, a matched one vanishes into the atom, the electron visibly jumps, and after a moment it falls back and re-emits
Energy ladder drawn to scale from E_n = -13.6 Z^2/n^2, with level labels nudged apart and led back to their lines so the crowding towards zero stays readable

Every absorbed photon leaves a dark line on a logarithmic spectrum strip banded X-ray, extreme UV, ultraviolet, visible and infrared, so the student sees that neither line in this question is visible light
Chart of transition energy against atomic number, showing the Z-squared law with the current sample marked on it
Ratio hunter: two ladders side by side, each locked to the transition the question gives it, with two atomic-number dials and a live wavelength ratio that only locks at exactly 9.0000
A sweep helper that walks Z_X upwards and stops itself the moment the ratio locks
Found-pair table showing that every solution is a multiple of (3, 2), with a + b growing for every multiple above the first
Charge counter: the ion drawn with countable protons and its single electron, a tally that converts protons and electrons into a and b, and the sum
An m study proving the minimum rather than asserting it - it stays blank until both ions have been counted, so it cannot print the answer to a student who is only scrolling
Seven expandable JEE traps, each phrased as the misconception a student actually holds, starting with the 3 + 2 = 5 error
Progressive four-level hint system on every bench, conceptual clue first and near-solution last
Progress bar, four earnable badges and an end-of-lab celebration reporting evidence collected and prediction accuracy
Auto play that walks the whole investigation, pausing at each prediction
Teacher mode with objectives, the expected wrong answers ranked, a teaching order and a discussion question
Answer gated until all four benches have been run, with a reveal-anyway escape
Step-by-step solution with an independent verification log
